- Use case: document summarization + long-form report generation with RAG for 10 internal teams.
- Next steps we discussed: provide average prompt & completion token counts, expected monthly requests, and how often you need extended context (8k vs 32k vs 128k).

Could you confirm the following numbers so I can finalize the estimate? If you don't have exact answers, ballpark ranges are fine.

1) Avg prompt tokens per request (including system + instruction + retrieved doc prefixes): ___
2) Avg completion tokens per request (model output): ___
3) Typical workload shape: expected requests/day and any peaks
4) Percent of requests that need 8k context vs 32k vs 128k
5) Target budget range and target $/1M tokens for procurement to hit (helps me propose plan tiers)

I've attached a draft pricing_estimate_v1.pdf with example unit economics for 8k/32k/128k so you can see how the units map to line items.

Hi Marissa - great notes, thanks. Below are the numbers from our analytics team (ballpark monthly averages, happy to share raw logs if useful):

1) Avg prompt tokens: 600 tokens (includes system prompt + top-k retrieved context snippets; prompt distribution is skewed - ~70% in 300-800 tokens)
2) Avg completion tokens: 1,200 tokens (most outputs are ~400-1,800, mean ~1,200)
3) Requests: ~25k requests/day on average (weekdays), ~15k weekends; expect spikes up to 80k/day during monthly reporting windows
   - Monthly baseline requests: ~700k requests/month
   - Monthly tokens (approx): (600+1,200)*700k ~= 1.26 billion tokens/month (note: this counts both prompt+completion tokens)
4) Context length needs: ~85% of requests only need 8k context; ~13% need 32k for longer report stitching; ~2% are potential 128k needs (very rare, for end-of-quarter archival reports)
5) Budget & target economics: procurement is looking at a budget band of $5k- $15k/month initially for a pilot; target unit economics is roughly $50/1M tokens (they flagged this as an internal target to hit for hosted pricing).

We can also provide a sample of raw prompt+completion token histograms if that helps your sizing. Let me know if you want the logs redacted first.

Thanks - Alice

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes & context-length needs

Thanks Alice - super helpful detail, especially the 1.26B tokens/mo estimate and the 8k/32k/128k split. A few notes and an initial commercial outline:

1) Quick math confirmation: your stated numbers imply ~1.26B tokens/month (prompt + completion). If you're targeting ~$50/1M tokens that maps to ~ $63k/month which is above the pilot budget band you mentioned - so there will be a couple product/commercial levers to explore (model selection, batching, prefix caching, and committed capacity).

2) Pricing (hosted, illustrative per 1M tokens):
   - 8k context model (standard): $45 / 1M tokens (baseline hosted SKU)
   - 32k context model (extended): $80 / 1M tokens
   - 128k context model (long-context): $150 / 1M tokens
   - Notes: these are ballpark published SKUs; committed / Dedicated capacity and quantized variants can be materially lower (we typically see 15-40% discounts on unit cost for Dedicated + commit).

3) Unit economics levers we recommend for you:
   - Serve the 85% 8k traffic on a standard SKU (reduces cost).
   - Use prefix/KV caching for repeated context blocks - should reduce prompt tokens by ~10-25% depending on retrieval strategy.
   - Batch and concurrency tuning at the client to reduce per-token runtime costs; can also move some jobs to Dedicated capacity for predictable pricing.

4) Example pilot proposal (to hit your $5k- $15k band):
   - 90-day pilot focusing on a subset of teams (cap monthly traffic to 10-15% of baseline) - expected consumption 120-200M tokens/month.
   - Host 8k traffic on standard SKU + enable caching. Estimated cost (hosted, mid-tier): $45/1M * 160M ~= $7,200/month (before discounts). With a 20% pilot discount = ~$5,760/month.

5) Next asks from my side:
   - If you can share a short token histogram (CSV) for a 1-week sample that captures per-request prompt and completion tokens, we'll run it through our pricing simulator and send a detailed line-item estimate.
   - Do you have an internal date for PO/approval if pilot goes well? Procurement cadence will drive committed pricing options.

I've attached a quick one-pager with the pilot outline (MA-plan.pdf). If this aligns, I can loop in our sales engineering team to build the sample runbook and a canned contract (SOW + one-month PO-friendly term).

Attachment: [MA-plan.pdf (PDF, 80KB)]

Thanks - happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk the numbers.
